about.text: Milk pumped at high pressure through a narrow gap, which breaks its fat globules so small that they stay spread through it instead of rising as a layer of cream. Homogenised milk is also whiter and tastes fuller.

sources.text: All made from whole milk: packaged milk, yoghurt and dahi, whole milk powder, khoa, paneer, and the ghee churned from dahi at home. What is left once the rest is counted.

how.text: Warm milk is pumped at high pressure through a narrow gap, which tears the fat globules into droplets under 1 µm. Droplets that small stay suspended, so no cream layer forms on top.

steps.note: Below 40 °C the fat is broken up poorly.
Pumped through a narrow gap at 100–250 bar (for example 200 bar), then a second stage at about 30 bar back-pressure.
